newsitem.title: POLAND: CIGNA ALLOWED TO BUY SMALL POLISH INSURERS.
newsitem.headline: CIGNA ALLOWED TO BUY SMALL POLISH INSURERS.

text.p: Poland's finance ministry has granted a permit for Cigna International, a unit of U.S. Cigna Corp., to buy into two small Polish insurance companies, the ministry said on Wednesday.
The ministry has allowed Cigna to buy a majority stake in life insurance firm STU Zycie SA and a minority equity of non-life insurer STU SA, said a spokewoman of the ministry, Anna Sobocinska.
The finance ministry issues licences for insurance operations in Poland, therefore foreign companies buying into existing insurance firms need its approval.
STU SA had a 0.3 percent market share at the end of 1996.
Private Polish trader Bartimpex and its subsidiary Bank Wschodnio-Europejski SA (BWE) now hold 80 percent of STU SA. STU Life is 35-percent owned by STU SA and 40-percent by BWE.
Bartimpex president Aleksander Gudzowaty said earlier this year his firm and BWE would remain investors in the two firms after the Cigna investment.
